open_points.subject: A17
open_points.text: a misspelt name still stops the start, as the item it was meant to set is then missing
open_points.question: When the only attempted service-token setting is a misspelt unknown variable, must Registry fail because a token was apparently intended, or ignore it and start owner-only because all four declared service tokens are absent?
options: Ignore the unknown variable and start owner-only when all four declared service-token items are absent.
Treat any unknown REGISTRY_ variable resembling a service-token item as an attempted partial service configuration and fail the start.
Make the statement about misspellings apply only to items that are unconditionally required, such as the backup key.
open_points.default_guess: Ignore every unknown variable exactly as rule 1 says and start owner-only when no correctly named service token is present.

witness.initial: All unconditionally required items are valid, no correctly named service token is set, and REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKENN is set instead of the PresuPro token's declared name.
events: Registry classifies the misspelt variable and checks whether the service-token group is all four or none.
outcomes: The misspelt name is ignored; none of the four declared tokens is present, so Registry starts owner-only.
The misspelling means an intended item is missing, so Registry stops the start and names the PresuPro token as missing.
witness.observer: The owner, and any service attempting to connect to the service API.

open_points.subject: A17
open_points.text:
a variable whose name names none of them —
   one beginning with `REGISTRY_` included — is neither read nor checked and
   does not stop the start
open_points.question: What Required tests item must show that every undeclared variable is neither read nor checked, rather than merely showing that the single name REGISTRY_EXTRA does not stop one start?
options: Require tests with multiple arbitrary undeclared names and values, plus evidence that the environment-reading boundary requests only declared items.
Narrow the normative rule to the single tested name REGISTRY_EXTRA.
Require only that arbitrary undeclared variables do not affect the externally observed start result, without claiming they are never read.
open_points.default_guess: Test arbitrary undeclared names and verify at the environment-reader boundary that only declared item names are accessed.

witness.initial: Every declared item is valid and an undeclared REGISTRY_OTHER variable is present.
events: An implementation either ignores every undeclared variable or special-cases only REGISTRY_EXTRA while rejecting other REGISTRY_ names.
The listed Required tests are run.
outcomes: Registry starts because REGISTRY_OTHER is undeclared and ignored.
Registry stops because REGISTRY_OTHER is rejected, although it still passes the listed test using REGISTRY_EXTRA.
witness.observer: The owner and the State 2 test suite.

open_points.subject: A17
open_points.question: Does config in this invariant mean the complete set of REGISTRY_ environment variables, including variables that must not be checked, or only the projection onto declared configuration items; and what does checks_passed mean for an unexamined variable?
options: config means only the declared-item projection; unknown variables are outside the invariant.
config includes every REGISTRY_ variable, and unknown variables pass vacuously without being read or checked.
Replace the invariant with one that explicitly quantifies only declared configuration items.
open_points.default_guess: Define config for this invariant as the declared-item projection and state that explicitly.

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: 2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: After the latest A17 change, is the security review reopened, and if so what are the new outcomes for every category that names A17 before A21 may again say the review is performed?
options: Re-review authentication_credential_abuse and secrets, record the review after this A17 change, and then close A21 if their outcomes remain valid.
Treat the existing 2026-11-11 review as covering this later A17 change and provide evidence establishing that ordering and coverage.
Leave A21 reopened and do not treat Security review: PERFORMED as current.
open_points.default_guess: Treat A21 as reopened and re-review authentication_credential_abuse and secrets before closing it.
